title: Opening of the 6 June 1982 session and recap of Friday
summary: Phil Schaap opens the Sunday session for the Jazz Oral History Project, recaps Benny Waters's childhood, and asks how his jazz career began in Philadelphia around 1918.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: It is Sunday afternoon, the 6th of June, 1982, about 20 minutes of three. And we're gonna continue talking with Benny Waters for the Jazz Oral History Project, archived at the Institute of Jazz Studies, Rutgers University in Newark. And my name is Phil Schaap. Benny, on Friday you brought you through the first 16 years or so of your life, through your years in Brighton, Maryland, through the time you spent in Haverford, through your early dabbilings in keyboardisms, your instrument that you received from your brother, the fact that you were involved with him when the whole family sort of gravitated to the Philadelphia area in a variety of activities including, you know, soprano sax duets at the church, military music as in the marches, the waltzes and various popular musics for dances, and of course the fact that you had received a musical education from him and had dabbled in looking at a saxophone instruction book and it continued. But now a different story, one that is more involved with the art we're thinking about, the art of jazz, is coming into play in your life here around 1918 with your activities in the Philadelphia area, and the one which you seem to place a very, very special accent on, the Charlie Miller orchestra. Why don't we pick - hold on for one second (adjusts recording equipment) - why don't we pick up the story right there with the beginnings of your active jazz career. You were, I guess, about 16 years of age, and you started playing away from your family, your older brother Clarence's band, and started dabbling in these units in Philadelphia. How many jazz bands were there in Philadelphia and how did they find out about you and how did you know you belonged with them?
